items.q: Using truth table, show that p v (q ^ r) is logically equivalent to (p v q) ^ (p v r).
items.answer: Build columns for p, q, r, q^r, p v (q^r), p v q, p v r, (p v q)^(p v r) across all 8 rows. In each row the column p v (q^r) matches the column (p v q)^(p v r) exactly (both reduce to the same truth value since OR distributes over AND). items.q: A kite is flying at a height of 120 m. A boy is flying it so the kite moves horizontally at 5 m/s. Find the rate at which the string is being paid out when 150 m of string is already out.
items.answer: Let x = horizontal distance, L = string length. L^2 = x^2 + 120^2 (height constant). When L=150, x = sqrt(150^2-120^2) = sqrt(22500-14400) = sqrt(8100) = 90. Differentiating L^2=x^2+14400: 2L dL/dt = 2x dx/dt, so dL/dt = (x/L) dx/dt = (90/150)*5 = 3. Final answer: string is paid out at 3 m/s.

items.q: (a) If y = sin^-1((1-x^2)/(1+x^2)), find dy/dx using the substitution x = tan(theta). (b) If x^2 + y^2 = log(xy), find dy/dx.
items.answer: (a) Put x=tan(theta). Then (1-x^2)/(1+x^2) = (1-tan^2 theta)/(1+tan^2 theta) = cos(2theta). So y = sin^-1(cos(2theta)) = sin^-1(sin(pi/2-2theta)) = pi/2-2theta = pi/2-2tan^-1(x). Therefore dy/dx = -2/(1+x^2). (b) Differentiate implicitly: 2x+2y(dy/dx) = (1/(xy)) * d/dx(xy) = (1/(xy))(y + x dy/dx) = 1/x + (1/y)(dy/dx). Rearranging: 2y(dy/dx) - (1/y)(dy/dx) = 1/x - 2x. (dy/dx)(2y-1/y) = 1/x-2x. dy/dx = (1/x-2x)/(2y-1/y) = y(1-2x^2)/(x(2y^2-1)). Final answer: (a) dy/dx = -2/(1+x^2). (b) dy/dx = y(1-2x^2)/(x(2y^2-1)).

points.p: Correct substitution x=tan(theta) reducing expression to cos(2theta)
Correct final answer for (a): dy/dx=-2/(1+x^2)
Correct implicit differentiation of log(xy)=x^2+y^2
Correct final simplified answer for (b)

items.q: (a) Evaluate the integral of 1/(x(x+1)) dx using partial fractions. (b) Evaluate the integral of e^x(1/x - 1/x^2) dx.
items.answer: (a) 1/(x(x+1)) = A/x + B/(x+1). 1 = A(x+1)+Bx. At x=0: A=1. At x=-1: -B=1, B=-1. Integral = integral of (1/x - 1/(x+1)) dx = log|x| - log|x+1| + c = log|x/(x+1)| + c. (b) Note that d/dx(e^x/x) = e^x/x - e^x/x^2 = e^x(1/x-1/x^2). So the integral directly equals e^x/x + c. Final answer: (a) log|x/(x+1)| + c. (b) e^x/x + c.

items.q: (a) Form the differential equation representing the family of curves y = A e^(3x) + B e^(-3x), where A and B are arbitrary constants. (b) Solve: x dy/dx + y = x^2, given y(1)=1.
items.answer: (a) y = A e^(3x) + B e^(-3x). Differentiating: y' = 3A e^(3x) - 3B e^(-3x). Differentiating again: y'' = 9A e^(3x) + 9B e^(-3x) = 9(A e^(3x)+B e^(-3x)) = 9y. So the required differential equation is y'' - 9y = 0. (b) Rewrite as dy/dx + y/x = x, linear with P=1/x, Q=x. I.F.=e^(integral of 1/x dx)=e^(log x)=x. Solution: y*x = integral of x*x dx = integral of x^2 dx = x^3/3 + c. So y = x^2/3 + c/x. Using y(1)=1: 1 = 1/3 + c, c=2/3. Final answer: (a) y''-9y=0. (b) y = x^2/3 + 2/(3x).

points.p: Correct two differentiations eliminating A and B to reach y''=9y
Correct final differential equation y''-9y=0
Correct identification of P, Q, I.F.=x and solution y*x=integral of x^2 dx
Correct use of initial condition to get c=2/3 and final y=x^2/3+2/(3x)

items.q: (a) State any two properties of a binomial distribution. (b) In a binomial distribution, the mean is 6 and variance is 3. Find n and p, and find P(X=0).
items.answer: (a) Two properties: the number of trials n is finite and fixed; each trial results in only two outcomes (success/failure) with constant probability p of success across all trials (also mean=np and variance=npq with npq<=np/4 always). (b) Mean=np=6, variance=npq=3. Dividing, q=npq/np=3/6=0.5, so p=1-q=0.5. Then n=6/p=6/0.5=12. P(X=0) = nC0 p^0 q^n = q^12 = (0.5)^12 = 1/4096. Final answer: (a) as listed above. (b) n=12, p=0.5, P(X=0)=1/4096.

points.p: Correctly stating two valid properties of binomial distribution
Correct equations np=6 and npq=3 set up
Correct calculation of q=0.5, p=0.5, n=12
Correct final P(X=0)=1/4096
